description: Fixture objects that are real wire instances but carry no `schema` discriminator, bound by exact JSON Pointer to the schema that owns them. check_declared_schema_fixture_instances only claims objects that name their own schema, so an instance without that member has no schema landing point at all: it survives every field deletion its schema makes, and the drift surfaces only when a downstream deny_unknown_fields type finally parses it. Each row makes one such object validate in the artifact pipeline instead.
registry_rules: pointer MUST resolve to an object in the named fixture; a stale row is a failure, not a silent skip
schema_ref MUST resolve through the shared schema resolver, fragment included

the instance MUST validate: this registry has no negative rows, because an intentionally invalid branch belongs in that fixture's own schema_validation_cases where its expected first error is testable
an object that already carries a `schema` discriminator MUST NOT be listed: it is already covered, and a second owner lets the two disagree

bindings.why: Embedded in the root-signed PCR genesis payload, so it is not an independently signed object and carries no schema member. Review 2026-09-02-1955 deleted device_key_digest and hpke_key_digest from the schema; this fixture kept shipping both until 2026-09-03.

The record is carried as an embedded JSON string, which is opaque to both the schema walk and additionalProperties. It kept a content_digest sibling that encoding.md 4.0.1 had already deleted from the schema, in the very commit that deleted it.

Vector input that is a real ServiceDescribe private_contact_discovery instance but sits inside a case input, so it names no schema member. Review 2026-09-05-0210: it carried a distribution member (and five profile-fixed parameters) that the closed describe schema rejects; the profile identity fixes those values, so they are not describe fields.
